correctness.rationale: A strictly increasing branch cannot interchange two of its own points. In a crossing cycle the left state satisfies 0<x≤min(b,c), and the strictly increasing right inverse forces a unique right state y=b+(1-b)(x/c)^(1/d). The scalar difference D between L and this inverse is therefore exact, including a possible zero at x=b=c and excluding x=0. Differentiation on the open domain reduces D'=0 to a level of [x^(1/d)(1-x/b)]^(1-d). The base increases to b/(d+1) and then decreases, so d≠1 yields at most two critical points; Rolle applies also between interior roots and an included endpoint. At the rational witness, an independent fraction check confirms D(0)=-1/20, D(3b/4)=-67/1960, D(b)=41/490 and the positive squared gap 168613/3841600 for D(b/4)>0. The three brackets give all roots and force all three to be simple, since two inter-root critical points already exhaust the bound. At a root the positive two-step multiplier satisfies μ-1=R'(L(x))D'(x); the signs +,-,+ give two repellers and an attractor. L(x)-x≥1/20, and y²≥4b(y-b) gives R(y)/y≤7/40 on the right. Both inequalities have a uniform positive fixed-point exclusion margin on their compact rescaled branch domains, using the continuous extension of the right formula at b only for that margin. The root brackets and margins persist on an open parameter set. At d=1,a=b=c the two branches are exact inverses on the listed crossing states, yielding the stated continuum.

value.rationale: The family is an established model introduced to study dynamics without equilibria. A sharp global census for its first nontrivial period, proved even when fixed points exist, and an open fixed-point-free realization with both attracting and repelling primitive cycles provide structural information absent from a fixed-point or numerical chaos study. The unrestricted affine exponent degeneration explains why the exponent hypothesis matters.
residual_risks: The result does not classify basins, rule out other periods, or prove chaos.
